messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert - high rate of trace export failures detected from OTEL-collector (project: inference-prod). 429/503 spikes to NewRelic exporter since 2026-03-15T09:12Z. Dropped spans ~92% over last 6m. Paging @sre-oncall.

alex (on-call): acknowledged, I'm on it. setting P1, paging SRE rotation. tagging #incidents.

maria (sre): seeing same in logs, otel-collector queue_full counter increasing. exporters/newrelic returned 429s + occasional 503s.

cheng (observability): confirmed. Honeycomb also shows elevated ingest backpressure earlier in the window, but current vendor errors correlate with NewRelic endpoints. attaching quick grep: 
```
grep -i "exporter" /var/log/otel/collector.log | tail -n 40
2026-03-15T09:11:40Z exporter newrelic: status=429 reason="rate limit"
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z exporter newrelic: status=503 reason="service_unavailable"
2026-03-15T09:12:18Z exporter newrelic: queue_full=true drop_spans=12034
```

alex (on-call): ok first priorities: stop further data loss for customers and notify CS. mitigation plan: 1) switch otel-collector to local file-buffered exporter plugin (enable fs_queue) 2) enable sampling at edge (reduce spans by 80%) 3) temporarily pause NewRelic exporter for non-critical tenants 4) open vendor ticket and cross-check status page. executing step 1 now.

ops-bot: runbook step executed: created incident ticket RED-2026-0315-ONCALL.

maria (sre): patch ready. sample config snippet below to enable filesystem queue and increase retry/backoff:
```
exporters:
  file_queue:
    path: "/var/lib/otel/queue"
    max_size: 1000000
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      exporters: [file_queue, newrelic]
```

alex (on-call): applying to inference-prod cluster now: `kubectl -n observability apply -f otel-fsqueue-patch.yaml`

cheng (observability): watching pods. collector rolling update started. log shows: `fs-queue: disk_buffer_enabled=true`

jessica (product): customer-ops, heads up - we should tell customers that traces may be delayed but not permanently lost while we buffer. which tenants affected?

customer-ops: high-usage tenants: acme-inc, shoploop, searchly. acme reported missing traces in incident form at 09:20. sending templated notice now. :mailbox_with_mail:

alex (on-call): enabling sampling rule for edge ingress to cut span volume: `otel-ctl set-sampling --rate 0.2 --selector "service=frontend*"` applied.

maria (sre): sampling took effect, spans/sec dropped ~78%. queue size draining to file buffer. exporter retries continue but error rate to NewRelic still ~25% of pre-mitigation.

cheng (observability): vendor status: https://status.newrelic.com/incidents/NR-2026-0315 shows ingest throttling for EU region; ETA unknown. opened ticket NR-78921 referencing our request id and logs.

alex (on-call): good. next, let's pause non-critical tenant exports to reduce pressure further. maria, can you patch pipeline to exclude non-prod tenants?

maria (sre): patch applied: non-prod exporters removed from pipeline. verifying.

ops-bot: deploy hook success: collectors in observability namespace now at revision v2.14.3-fsqueue.

customer-ops: sent initial customer notification to affected customers, support triage on standby.

cheng (observability): while vendor recovers, we should persist buffered files to durable S3 every 10m to avoid local disk OOM in case of prolonged outage. I'll create a small lambda to ship files to S3 and then to reingest when NR accepts.

alex (on-call): agreed. maria, please add scheduled job to ship buffer -> s3. sample command: `aws s3 cp /var/lib/otel/queue s3://redwood-otel-buffer/inference-prod/ --recursive`

maria (sre): scheduled via cronjob, starting in 5m.

cheng (observability): quick checks: tracing visibility resumed for most requests in UI (delayed by buffer), we can see backfilled spans for requests processed after 09:25.

jessica (product): what's customer impact level? is this causing errors in customer-facing apps?

alex (on-call): impact: no service downtime; only observability/traces degraded or delayed. A few customers reported missing traces which should be backfilled from buffer. severity: moderate (observability only), flagged P1 because cross-tenant telemetry loss.

incident-bot: Incident RED-2026-0315-ONCALL acknowledged by alex. escalation: paged on-call SRE.

maria (sre): NewRelic support replied: they're throttling ingestion for our org due to sudden spike, gave soft-limit and recommended batching + backoff. they expect partial recovery within 2h.

alex (on-call): ok we'll keep buffering + sampling + S3 offload. update tickets and close if stable.

cheng (observability): monitoring: set alert when fs_queue disk usage > 70% and S3 offload fails. added dashboard panel.

ops-bot: metrics: span_drop_rate decreased from 92% -> 6% after mitigations.

customer-ops: CS updated customers at 10:07 with expected timeline. no escalations yet.

maria (sre): around 11:05 vendor reports recovery. NewRelic ingest 200 responses resumed. retry loop successfully delivered buffered items. observed backfill throughput ~1500 traces/sec.

alex (on-call): verifying. rescan logs: exporter 200s for last 20m, queue drained to <1%.

incident-bot: Incident RED-2026-0315-ONCALL resolved by alex (on-call). duration 02:03:00.

jessica (product): thanks team. we'll open a postmortem ticket and propose persistent fs-queue + S3 offload as standard for critical clusters.

cheng (observability): noted follow-ups: 1) long-term: implement OTLP backpressure handling improvements and honor Retry-After, 2) add vendor rate-limit guardrails (client-side throttling per-tenant), 3) add synthetic trace checks to detect export gaps faster.

alex (on-call): handoff to next oncall @maria for the remainder of the day. leaving notes in RED-2026-0315-ONCALL. :thumbsup:

maria (sre): taking handoff. I'll monitor for 2h and then transition to normal ops.

customer-ops: follow-up: all affected customers have been notified that traces were backfilled and dashboards are recovering :raised_hands:.

jessica (product): assigning PM/owner for postmortem: jessica -> will draft and share within 24h.

cheng (observability): closing thread, migrating artifacts to confluence page: https://redwood.atl/incident/RED-2026-0315-otel-exporting-lag

alex (on-call): thanks everyone. good job moving fast and protecting customer data.
